commit_message:
Bug 1941826: Don't guard for number types in emitGuardIsNumber. r=jandem

This aligns Warp transpilation with CacheIR, because in CacheIR `NumberOperandId`
can mean either `Double` or `Int32`. (There isn't yet an explicit
`DoubleOperandId` to denote a value is guaranteed to be a Double.)

Float32 optimisations can be more easily applied when `MToDouble` isn't emitted
and we also no longer need the `MToDouble::canProduceFloat32` override added in
D215775.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D234348

fix_commit.message: Bug 1942648: Support MSign with Int32 input and Double output. r=jandem
fix_commit.author: André Bargull

findings.title: Missing type conversion case in visitSign causes JIT type confusion
findings.message: The change to emitGuardIsNumber removed automatic conversion of Int32/Float32 inputs to Double. This broke an implicit assumption in visitSign that when input and output types differ, the input is always Double and output is Int32. When MSign now receives Int32 input with Double output, the else branch incorrectly asserts the opposite and uses LSignDI (Double input, Int32 output) instead of a proper LSignID (Int32 input, Double output). This causes: 1) Writing to an unrelated general purpose register instead of the allocated float output register, 2) The allocated float register retains its previous value, enabling type confusion where uninitialized/stale float data can be read as legitimate values.
findings.suggestion: When removing the automatic type conversion in emitGuardIsNumber, all downstream consumers that rely on specific type combinations need to be audited and updated. The visitSign function in Lowering.cpp needs to handle the new case where input is Int32 and output is Double by adding a new LIR instruction (LSignID) and corresponding code generation.

findings.title: Incomplete type handling in LIRGenerator::visitSign
findings.message: The visitSign function only handles two cases: (1) same input/output types, and (2) Double input with Int32 output. After the change in emitGuardIsNumber, a third case became possible: Int32 input with Double output. The assertions at lines 2100-2101 assume the impossible third case cannot happen, but it now can. When this case is hit, the code incorrectly creates an LSignDI instruction (for Double->Int32) when it should create an LSignID instruction (for Int32->Double). This register type mismatch leads to writing to wrong registers and type confusion.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit handling for the Int32 input / Double output case by creating a new LSignID LIR instruction and corresponding CodeGenerator visitor. The fix should enumerate all four possible type combinations explicitly rather than relying on implicit assumptions.

ground_truth.root_cause: The change in emitGuardIsNumber (bug 1941826) removed automatic conversion of Int32/Float32 inputs to Double for number guards. This was intended to enable better Float32 optimizations. However, downstream code in visitSign had hardcoded assumptions that when MSign input and output types differ, the input is always Double and output is Int32. The change created a new valid case (Int32 input, Double output) that was not handled, causing assertion failures and type confusion when the wrong LIR instruction was selected.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable change that removed automatic Int32/Float32 to Double conversion. When IsNumberType(def->type()) returns true for Int32, the function now returns early without converting to Double, breaking the postcondition that downstream code expects.

Creates MSign instruction with NumberOperandId input and Int32 output type. This function relies on emitGuardIsNumber to ensure proper type handling, and passes the incorrectly-typed operand to the MSign constructor, propagating the type confusion to the lowering phase.

Contains the broken assumption at lines 2188-2192. When input type differs from output type and output is Int32, the code assumes input MUST be Double and creates LSignDI instruction. This assumption is violated when emitGuardIsNumber allows Int32 to pass through, causing wrong LIR instruction selection (LSignDI expects Double input but receives Int32), leading to wrong register writes and type confusion.
